definitions.DOG: A mammal, Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris, that has been domesticated for thousands of years, of highly variable appearance due to human breeding.
definitions.CAT: An animal of the family Felidae:.
definitions.BIRD: A member of the class of animals Aves in the phylum Chordata, characterized by being warm-blooded, having feathers and wings usually capable of flight, and laying eggs.
definitions.FISH: A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water, moving with the help of fins and breathing with gills.
definitions.LION: A big cat, Panthera leo, native to Africa, India and formerly much of Europe.
definitions.TIGER: Panthera tigris, a large predatory mammal of the cat family, indigenous to Asia.
definitions.BEAR: A large omnivorous mammal, related to the dog and raccoon, having shaggy hair, a very small tail, and flat feet.
definitions.WOLF: The gray wolf, specifically all subspecies of the gray wolf (Canis lupus) that are not dingoes or dogs.
definitions.DEER: A ruminant mammal with antlers and hooves of the family Cervidae, or one of several similar animals from related families of the order Artiodactyla.
definitions.HORSE: Any of several animals related to Equus ferus caballus.
definitions.PIG: Any of several intelligent mammalian species of the genus Sus, having cloven hooves, bristles and a nose adapted for digging.
definitions.GOAT: A mammal, Capra aegagrus hircus, and similar species of the genus Capra.
definitions.SHEEP: A woolly ruminant of the genus Ovis.
definitions.DUCK: To quickly lower the head or body in order to prevent it from being struck by something.
definitions.GOOSE: Any of various grazing waterfowl of the family Anatidae, which have feathers and webbed feet and are capable of flying, swimming, and walking on land, and which are bigger than ducks.
definitions.SWAN: Any of various species of large, long-necked waterfowl, of genus Cygnus (bird family: Anatidae), most of which have white plumage.
definitions.EAGLE: Any of several large carnivorous and carrion-eating birds in the family Accipitridae, having a powerful hooked bill and keen vision.
definitions.HAWK: A diurnal predatory bird of the family Accipitridae, smaller than an eagle.
definitions.OWL: Any of various birds of prey of the order Strigiformes that are primarily nocturnal and have forward-looking, binocular vision, limited eye movement, and good hearing.
definitions.MOUSE: Any small rodent of the genus Mus.
definitions.RAT: A medium-sized rodent belonging to the genus Rattus.
definitions.BAT: Any of the flying mammals of the order Chiroptera, usually small and nocturnal, insectivorous or frugivorous.
definitions.APE: A primate of the clade Hominoidea, generally larger than monkeys and distinguished from them by having no tail.
definitions.LLAMA: A South American mammal of the camel family, Lama glama, used as a domestic beast of burden and a source of wool and meat.
definitions.CAMEL: A beast of burden, much used in desert areas, of the genus Camelus.
definitions.PONY: A small horse; specifically, any of several small breeds of horse under 14.2 hands at the withers.
definitions.BUCK: A male deer, antelope, or rabbit.
definitions.DOE: A female deer, rabbit, or hare.
definitions.CUB: A young bear, lion, fox, or wolf.
definitions.PUG: A small breed of dog with a wrinkled face and curled tail.
definitions.HEN: A female chicken (Gallus gallus), particularly a sexually mature one kept for its eggs.
definitions.MULE: The generally sterile male or female hybrid offspring of a male donkey and a female horse.
definitions.ELK: Any of various large species of deer such as the red deer, moose or wapiti (see usage notes).
definitions.MOOSE: The largest member of the deer family (Alces americanus, sometimes included in Alces alces), of which the male has very large, palmate antlers.
definitions.LYNX: Any of several medium-sized wild cats, mostly of the genus Lynx.
definitions.PUMA: The mountain lion or cougar, Puma concolor.
definitions.KOALA: A tree-dwelling marsupial, Phascolarctos cinereus, that resembles a small bear with a broad head, large ears and sharp claws, mainly found in eastern Australia.
definitions.BADGER: Any mammal of three subfamilies, which belong to the family Mustelidae: Melinae (Eurasian badgers), Mellivorinae (ratel or honey badger), and Taxideinae (American badger).
definitions.SKUNK: Any of various small mammals, of the family Mephitidae, native to North and Central America, having a glossy black with a white coat and two musk glands at the base of the tail for emitting a noxious smell as a defensive measure.
definitions.ROOK: A black bird of the crow family.
definitions.CROW: A large black bird known for its intelligence and cawing call.
definitions.DOVE: A bird of the pigeon family, symbol of peace.
definitions.LARK: A small songbird known for its melodious singing.
definitions.FINCH: A small seed-eating songbird with a short, stout bill.
definitions.JAY: A colorful, noisy bird of the crow family.
definitions.HERON: A large wading bird with long legs and a long neck.
definitions.CRANE: Any bird of the family Gruidae, large birds with long legs and a long neck which is extended during flight.
definitions.IBIS: A large wading bird with a long, curved bill.
definitions.SWIFT: A fast-flying bird similar to a swallow.
definitions.ROBIN: A small songbird with a reddish-breast.
definitions.SNIPE: A wading bird with a very long, slender bill.
definitions.TERN: A seabird resembling a gull, with a forked tail.
definitions.PUFFIN: A colorful seabird known for its nesting habits.
definitions.ELEPHANT: A mammal of the order Proboscidea, having a trunk, and two large ivory tusks jutting from the upper jaw.
definitions.GIRAFFE: A ruminant, of the genus Giraffa, of the African savannah with long legs and highly elongated neck, which make it the tallest living animal; yellow fur patterned with dark spots, often in the form of a network; and two or more short, skin-covered horns, so-called; strictly speaking the horn-like projections are ossicones.
definitions.KANGAROO: A member of the Macropodidae family of large marsupials with strong hind legs for hopping, native to Australia.
definitions.PENGUIN: Any of several flightless sea birds, of order Sphenisciformes, found in the Southern Hemisphere, marked by their usual upright stance, walking on short legs, and (generally) their stark black and white plumage.
definitions.DOLPHIN: A carnivorous aquatic mammal in one of several families of order Cetacea, famed for its intelligence and occasional willingness to approach humans.
definitions.WHALE: Any of several species of large sea mammals of the infraorder Cetacea.
definitions.SHARK: A scaleless, predatory fish of the superorder Selachimorpha, with a cartilaginous skeleton and 5 to 7 gill slits on each side of its head.
definitions.TURTLE: Any land or marine reptile of the order Testudines, characterised by a protective shell enclosing its body.
definitions.RABBIT: A mammal of the family Leporidae, with long ears, long hind legs and a short, fluffy tail.
definitions.HAMSTER: Any of various Old-World rodent species belonging to the subfamily Cricetinae.
definitions.LEOPARD: Panthera pardus, a large wild cat with a spotted coat native to Africa and Asia, especially the male of the species (in contrast to leopardess).
definitions.CHEETAH: A distinctive member (Acinonyx jubatus) of the cat family, slightly smaller than the leopard, but with proportionately longer limbs and a smaller head.
definitions.PANTHER: Any of various big cats with black fur; most especially, the black-coated leopard of India.
definitions.GORILLA: The largest of the apes, native to the forests of central Africa, and known for their trait of knuckle-walking.
definitions.CHIMPANZEE: A species of great ape in the genus Pan, native to Africa, and believed by biologists to be the closest extant relative to humans.
definitions.ORANGUTAN: An arboreal anthropoid ape genus Pongo consisting of two species, Pongo pygmaeus of Borneo and Pongo abelii of Sumatra, having a shaggy reddish-brown coat, long arms, and no tail.
definitions.BABOON: An Old World monkey of the genus Papio, having dog-like muzzles and large canine teeth, cheek pouches, a short tail, and naked callosities on the buttocks.
definitions.MONKEY: Any member of the clade Simiiformes not also of the clade Hominoidea containing humans and apes, from which they are usually, but not universally, distinguished by smaller size, a tail, and cheek pouches.
definitions.LEMUR: Any strepsirrhine primate of the infraorder Lemuriformes, superfamily Lemuroidea, native only to Madagascar and some surrounding islands.
definitions.SLOTH: Laziness; slowness in the mindset; disinclination to action or labour.
definitions.PLATYPUS: A semi-aquatic, egg-laying monotreme mammal with a bill resembling that of a duck, that has a mole-like body, a tail resembling that of a beaver, a waterproof pelt, and flat webbed feet — males have poisonous spurs on the inside of the back legs; Ornithorhynchus anatinus.
definitions.ECHIDNA: Any of the species of small spined monotremes in family Tachyglossidae, the four extant species of which are found in Australia and southern New Guinea.
definitions.WALLABY: Any of several species of marsupial; usually smaller and stockier than kangaroos.
definitions.WOMBAT: Any of several herbivorous, burrowing marsupials, of the family Vombatidae, mainly found in southern and eastern Australia.
definitions.BANDICOOT: A small Australian marsupial with a distinctive long snout, of the family Peramelidae.
definitions.QUOKKA: A cat-sized marsupial, Setonix brachyurus, of southwestern Australia.
definitions.DINGO: Canis lupus dingo, a wild dog native to Australia.
definitions.BILBY: Australian desert marsupial (Macrotis lagotis), with distinctive large ears and approximately the size of a rabbit.
definitions.JAGUAR: A carnivorous spotted large cat native to South and Central America, Panthera onca.
definitions.HYENA: Any of the medium-sized to large feliform carnivores of the subfamily Hyaeninae (genera Hyaena and Crocuta), native to Africa and Asia and noted for the sound similar to laughter which they can make if excited.
definitions.ZEBRA: Any of three species of genus Equus: E.
definitions.ANTELOPE: Any of several African mammals of the family Bovidae distinguished by hollow horns, which, unlike deer, they do not shed.
definitions.GAZELLE: An antelope of either of the genera Gazella (mostly native to Africa) or Procapra (native to Asia), capable of running at high speeds for long periods.
definitions.MEERKAT: Suricata suricatta, a small carnivorous mammal of the mongoose family, from the Kalahari Desert, known for its habit of standing on its hind legs.
definitions.OTTER: An aquatic or marine carnivorous mammal in the subfamily Lutrinae of the family Mustelidae, which also includes weasels, polecats, badgers, and others.
definitions.BEAVER: A semiaquatic rodent of the genus Castor, having a wide, flat tail and webbed feet.
definitions.SQUIRREL: Any of the rodents of the family Sciuridae distinguished by their large bushy tail.
definitions.CHIPMUNK: A squirrel-like rodent of the genus Tamias, native mainly to North America.
definitions.RACCOON: A nocturnal omnivore native to North America, typically with a mixture of gray, brown, and black fur, a mask-like marking around the eyes and a striped tail; Procyon lotor.
definitions.ARMADILLO: Any of the burrowing mammals covered with bony, jointed, protective plates, order Cingulata, found in the Americas, especially in South America.
definitions.OPOSSUM: Any American marsupial of the family Didelphidae.
definitions.WALRUS: A large Arctic marine mammal related to seals and having long tusks, tough, wrinkled skin, and four flippers, Odobenus rosmarus.
definitions.SEAL: A pinniped (Pinnipedia), particularly an earless seal (true seal) or eared seal.
definitions.MANATEE: Any of several plant-eating marine mammals, of family Trichechidae, found in tropical regions.
definitions.DUGONG: A plant-eating aquatic marine mammal, of the genus Dugong, found in tropical regions.
definitions.NARWHAL: Monodon monoceros, an Arctic cetacean that grows to about 20 feet (6 meters) long, the male having a single horn-like tusk, a twisted, pointed canine tooth that projects forward.
definitions.ORCA: A sea mammal (Orcinus orca) related to dolphins and porpoises, commonly called the killer whale.
definitions.BELUGA: A cetacean, Delphinapterus leucas, found in the Arctic Ocean.
definitions.STINGRAY: Any of various large, venomous rays, of the orders Rajiformes and Myliobatiformes, having a barbed, whiplike tail.
definitions.OCTOPUS: Any of several marine molluscs of the family Octopodidae, having no internal or external protective shell or bone (unlike the nautilus, squid and cuttlefish) and eight arms each covered with suckers.
definitions.SQUID: Any of several carnivorous marine cephalopod mollusks, of the order Teuthida, having a mantle, eight arms, and a pair of tentacles.
definitions.LOBSTER: A crustacean of the Nephropidae family, dark green or blue-black in colour turning bright red when cooked, with a hard shell and claws, which is used as a seafood.
definitions.CRAB: A crustacean of the infraorder Brachyura, having five pairs of legs, the foremost of which are in the form of claws, and a carapace.
definitions.SHRIMP: Any of many swimming, often edible crustaceans, chiefly of the infraorder Caridea or the suborder Dendrobranchiata, with slender legs, long whiskers and a long abdomen.
definitions.STARFISH: Any of various asteroids or other echinoderms (not in fact fish) with usually five arms, many of which eat bivalves or corals by everting their stomach.
definitions.JELLYFISH: An almost transparent aquatic animal; any one of the acalephs, especially one of the larger species, having a jellylike appearance.
definitions.CORAL: A hard substance made of the limestone skeletons of marine polyps.
definitions.SPONGE: Any of various marine invertebrates, mostly of the phylum Porifera, that have a porous skeleton often of silica.
definitions.ANEMONE: Any plant of the genus Anemone, of the Ranunculaceae (or buttercup) family, such as the windflower.
definitions.FROG: A small tailless amphibian of the order Anura that typically hops.
definitions.TOAD: An amphibian, a kind of frog (order Anura) with shorter hindlegs and a drier, wartier skin, many in family Bufonidae.
definitions.NEWT: A small lizard-like amphibian in the family Salamandridae that lives in the water as an adult.
definitions.SALAMANDER: A long, slender, chiefly terrestrial amphibian of the order Caudata, superficially resembling a lizard.
definitions.LIZARD: Any reptile of the order Squamata that is not a snake, usually having four legs, external ear openings, movable eyelids and a long slender body and tail.
definitions.SNAKE: A legless reptile of the sub-order Serpentes with a long, thin body and a fork-shaped tongue.
definitions.TORTOISE: Any of various land-dwelling reptiles, of the family Testudinidae or the order Testudines , whose body is enclosed in a shell (carapace plus plastron).
definitions.IGUANA: A green iguana (Iguana iguana), a large tropical American lizard often kept as a pet.
definitions.GECKO: Any lizard of the family Gekkonidae.
definitions.CHAMELEON: A small to mid-size reptile, of the family Chamaeleonidae, and one of the best known lizard families able to change color and project its long tongue.
definitions.PYTHON: A type of large constricting snake.
definitions.COBRA: Any of various venomous snakes of the family Elapidae.
definitions.VIPER: A venomous snake in the family Viperidae.
definitions.DRAGON: A legendary serpentine or reptilian creature.
definitions.PHOENIX: A mythological bird, said to be the only one of its kind, which lives for 500 years and then dies by burning to ashes on a pyre of its own making, ignited by the sun.
definitions.UNICORN: A mythical beast resembling a horse or deer with a single, straight, spiraled horn projecting from its forehead.
definitions.GRIFFIN: A mythical beast having the body of a lion and the wings and head of an eagle.
definitions.PEGASUS: A winged horse fabled to have sprung from the body of Medusawhen she was slain.

definitions.BOAT: A craft used for transportation of goods, fishing, racing, recreational cruising, or military use on or in the water, propelled by oars or outboard motor or inboard motor or by wind.
definitions.SHIP: A water-borne vessel generally larger than a boat.
definitions.SAIL: A piece of fabric spread to catch the wind and propel a vessel.
definitions.MAST: A tall upright post on a ship or boat, carrying sails.
definitions.DECK: A flat covered surface that forms a floor on a ship.
definitions.HULL: The watertight body of a ship or boat.
definitions.PORT: The left side of a ship when facing forward.
definitions.BOW: The front end of a ship.
definitions.RIVER: A large and often winding stream which drains a land mass, carrying water down from higher areas to a lower point, oftentimes ending in another body of water, such as an ocean or in an inland sea.
definitions.LAKE: A small stream of running water; a channel for water; a drain.
definitions.OCEAN: One of the large bodies of water separating the continents.
definitions.WAVE: To move back and forth repeatedly and somewhat loosely.
definitions.TIDE: The periodic change of the sea level, particularly when caused by the gravitational influence of the sun and the moon.
definitions.SURF: Waves that break on an ocean shoreline.
definitions.FISH: A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water, moving with the help of fins and breathing with gills.
definitions.GULL: A seabird of the genus Larus or of the family Laridae.
definitions.YACHT: A sailboat or motorboat used for cruising or racing.
definitions.CANOE: A lightweight narrow boat, typically pointed at both ends, propelled by paddles.
definitions.KAYAK: A small, narrow watercraft propelled by a double-bladed paddle.
definitions.RAFT: A flat buoyant structure of timber, barrels, or other materials used for transport.
definitions.DOCK: A platform or structure extending into the water for vessels to tie up.
definitions.PIER: A platform supported on pillars, leading out into the water.
definitions.BUOY: An anchored float serving as a navigation mark or warning.
definitions.KNOT: A unit of speed equal to one geographical mile per hour.
definitions.ANCHOR: A heavy metal device cast overboard to keep a vessel in place.
definitions.CREW: The group of people who work on and operate a ship or boat.
definitions.WATER: A substance (of molecular formula H₂O) found at room temperature and pressure as a clear liquid.
definitions.BEACH: The shore of a body of water, especially when sandy or pebbly.
definitions.SAND: Rock that is ground more finely than gravel, but is not as fine as silt (more formally, see grain sizes chart), forming beaches and deserts and also used in construction.
definitions.SHELL: A hard external covering of an animal.
definitions.SHORE: Land adjoining a non-flowing body of water, such as an ocean, lake or pond.
definitions.COAST: The edge of the land where it meets an ocean, sea, gulf, bay, or large lake.
definitions.SEA: A large body of salt water.
definitions.HOOK: A rod bent into a curved shape, typically with one end free and the other end secured to a rope or other attachment.
definitions.NET: A figure made up of a large number of straight lines or curves,which are connected at certain points and related to each other bysome specified law.
definitions.BAIT: Any substance, especially food, used in catching fish, or other animals, by alluring them to a hook, snare, trap, or net.
definitions.OAR: A type of lever used to propel a boat, having a flat blade at one end and a handle at the other, and pivoted in a rowlock atop the gunwale, whereby a rower seated in the boat and pulling the handle can pass the blade through the water by repeated strokes against the water's resistance, thus moving the boat .
definitions.ROAM: To wander or travel freely and with no specific destination.
definitions.FLOW: A movement in people or things with a particular way in large numbers or amounts.
definitions.CABIN: A small dwelling characteristic of the frontier, especially when built from logs with simple tools and not constructed by professional builders, but by those who meant to live in it.
definitions.PADDLE: A two-handed, single-bladed oar used to propel a canoe or a small boat.
definitions.FERRY: A ship used to transport people, smaller vehicles and goods from one port to another, usually on a regular schedule.
definitions.BARGE: A large flat-bottomed towed or self-propelled boat used mainly for river and canal transport of heavy goods or bulk cargo.
definitions.STREAM: A small, narrow river of flowing water.
definitions.CREEK: A small inlet or bay, often saltwater, narrower and extending farther into the land than a cove; a recess in the shore of the sea, or of a river; the inner part of a port that is used as a dock for small boats.
definitions.BROOK: To use; enjoy; have the full employment of.
definitions.POND: An inland body of standing water, either natural or man-made, that is smaller than a lake.
definitions.CORAL: A hard substance made of the limestone skeletons of marine polyps.
definitions.REEF: A chain or range of rocks, sand, or coral lying at or near the surface of the water.
definitions.FLOAT: A buoyant device used to support something in water or another liquid.
definitions.DRIFT: (physical) Movement; that which moves or is moved.
definitions.SPRAY: A fine, gentle, dispersed mist of liquid.
definitions.MIST: Water or other liquid finely suspended in air.
definitions.DEEP: (with "the") The deep part of a lake, sea, etc.
definitions.BLUE: The colour of the clear sky or the deep sea, between green and violet in the visible spectrum, and one of the primary additive colours for transmitted light; the colour obtained by subtracting red and green from white light using magenta and cyan filters; or any colour resembling this.
definitions.SALT: A common substance, chemically consisting mainly of sodium chloride (NaCl), used extensively as a condiment and preservative.
definitions.CARGO: Freight carried by a ship, aircraft, or motor vehicle.
definitions.STERN: The back or rear end of a ship.
definitions.RIG: The rigging of a sailing ship or other such craft.
definitions.ROPE: Thick strings, yarn, monofilaments, metal wires, or strands of other cordage that are twisted together to form a stronger line.
definitions.LINE: A path through two or more points (compare ‘segment’); a continuous mark, including as made by a pen; any path, curved or straight.
definitions.NAVY: A country's entire sea force, including ships and personnel.
definitions.MARINE: A soldier, normally a member of a marine corps, trained to serve on board or from a ship.
definitions.VALVE: A device that controls the flow of a gas or fluid through a pipe.
definitions.PUMP: A device for moving or compressing a liquid or gas.
definitions.WHARF: A man-made landing place for ships on a shore or river bank.
definitions.JETTY: A structure of wood or stone extended into the sea to influence the current or tide, or to protect a harbor or beach.
definitions.QUAY: A stone or concrete structure on navigable water used for loading and unloading vessels; a wharf.
definitions.LOCK: Something used for fastening, which can only be opened with a key or combination.
definitions.CANAL: An artificial waterway or artificially improved river used for travel, shipping, or irrigation.
definitions.BASIN: A wide bowl for washing, sometimes affixed to a wall.
definitions.COVE: A hollow in a rock; a cave or cavern.
definitions.GULF: A hollow place in the earth; an abyss; a deep chasm or basin.
definitions.STRAIT: A narrow channel of water connecting two larger bodies of water.
definitions.CHANNEL: The physical confine of a river or slough, consisting of a bed and banks.
definitions.FJORD: A long, narrow, deep inlet between cliffs.
definitions.MARSH: An area of low, wet land, often with tall grass.
definitions.SWAMP: A piece of wet, spongy land; low ground saturated with water; soft, wet ground which may have a growth of certain kinds of trees, but is unfit for agricultural or pastoral purposes.
definitions.DELTA: The fourth letter of the modern Greek alphabet Δ, δ.
definitions.LAGOON: A shallow body of water separated from deeper sea by a bar.
definitions.ISLE: A wing of a building, notably in a church separated from the nave proper by piers.
definitions.SHOAL: A sandbank or sandbar creating a shallow.
definitions.BEACON: A signal fire to notify of the approach of an enemy, or to give any notice, commonly of warning.
definitions.LIGHTHOUSE: A tower or other structure exhibiting a light or lights to warn or guide sailors.
definitions.RUDDER: An underwater vane used to steer a vessel.
definitions.TILLER: A person who tills; a farmer.
definitions.COMPASS: A magnetic or electronic device used to determine the cardinal directions (usually magnetic or true north).
definitions.RADAR: A method of detecting distant objects and determining their position, velocity, or other characteristics by analysis of sent radio waves (usually microwaves) reflected from their surfaces.
definitions.GALLEY: A long, slender ship propelled primarily by oars, whether having masts and sails or not; usually referring to rowed warships used in the Mediterranean from the 16th century until the modern era.
definitions.BUNK: One of a series of berths or beds placed in tiers.
definitions.BILGE: The rounded portion of a ship's hull, forming a transition between the bottom and the sides.

definitions.WIFE: A married woman, especially in relation to her spouse.
definitions.AUNT: The sister or sister-in-law of one’s parent.
definitions.SISTER: A daughter of the same parents as another person; a female sibling.
definitions.BABY: A very young human, particularly from birth to a couple of years old or until walking is fully mastered.
definitions.NIECE: A daughter of one’s sibling, brother-in-law, or sister-in-law; either the daughter of one's brother ("fraternal niece"), or of one's sister ("sororal niece").
definitions.COUSIN: The child of a person's uncle or aunt.
definitions.UNCLE: The brother or brother-in-law of one’s parent.
definitions.MOTHER: A (human) female who has given birth to a baby.
definitions.FATHER: A (generally human) male who begets a child.
definitions.BROTHER: Son of the same parents as another person.
definitions.CHILD: A person who has not yet reached adulthood, whether natural (puberty), cultural (initiation), or legal (majority).
definitions.KIN: Persons of the same race or family.
definitions.FOLKS: A grouping of smaller peoples or tribes as a nation.
definitions.TWIN: Either of two people (or, less commonly, animals) who shared the same uterus at the same time.
definitions.ELDER: An older person or an older member, usually a leader, of some community.
definitions.GIRL: A female child, adolescent, or a young woman.
definitions.NEPHEW: A son of one's sibling, brother-in-law, or sister-in-law.
definitions.HEIR: Someone who inherits, or is designated to inherit, the property of another.
definitions.FAMILY: A group of people who are closely related to one another (by blood, marriage or adoption).
definitions.PARENT: One of the two persons from whom one is immediately biologically descended.
definitions.SPOUSE: A person in a marriage or marital relationship.
definitions.ADULT: A fully grown human or animal.
definitions.YOUTH: The quality or state of being young.
definitions.INFANT: A very young human being, from birth to somewhere between six months and two years of age, needing almost constant care and/or attention.
definitions.NEIGHBOR: A person living on adjacent or nearby land.
definitions.FRIEND: A person other than a family member, spouse or lover whose company one enjoys and towards whom one feels affection.
definitions.GUEST: A recipient of hospitality, specifically someone staying by invitation at the house of another.
definitions.HOST: One which receives or entertains a guest, socially, commercially, or officially.
definitions.BRIDE: A woman in the context of her own wedding; one who is going to marry or has just been married.
definitions.GROOM: A man who is about to marry.
definitions.WIDOW: A woman whose spouse has died (and who has not remarried); feminine of widower.
definitions.SIBLING: A person who shares a parent; one's brother or sister who one shares a parent with.
definitions.POPPY: Any plant of the genus Papaver or the family Papaveraceae, with crumpled, often red, petals and a milky juice having narcotic properties.
definitions.MUMMY: An embalmed human or animal corpse wrapped in linen bandages for burial, especially as practised by the ancient Egyptians and some Native American tribes.
definitions.ANCESTOR: One from whom a person is descended, whether on the father's or mother's side, at any distance of time; a progenitor; a forefather.
definitions.LINEAGE: Descent in a line from a common progenitor; progeny; descending line of offspring or ascending line of parentage.
definitions.DESCENDANT: One who is the progeny of a specified person, at any distance of time or through any number of generations.
definitions.RELATIVE: Someone in the same family; someone connected by blood, marriage, or adoption.
definitions.CLAN: A group of people all descended from a common ancestor, in fact or belief.
definitions.TRIBE: A socially, ethnically, or politically cohesive group of people.
definitions.HOUSEHOLD: Collectively, all the persons who live in a given house; a family including attendants, servants etc.; a domestic or family establishment.
definitions.GENEALOGY: The descent of a person, family, or group from an ancestor or ancestors; lineage or pedigree.
definitions.MATRIARCH: A female leader of a family, a tribe or an ethnic or religious group.
definitions.PATRIARCH: The highest form of bishop, in the ancient world having authority over other bishops in the province but now generally as an honorary title; in Roman Catholicism, considered a bishop second only to the Pope in rank.
definitions.STEPBROTHER: The son of one's stepparent who is not the son of either of one's biological parents.
definitions.STEPSISTER: The daughter of one's stepparent who is not the daughter of either of one's parents.
definitions.GUARDIAN: Someone who guards, watches over, or protects.
definitions.NURTURE: The act of nourishing or nursing; tender care.
definitions.CHERISH: To treat with affection, care, and tenderness; to nurture or protect with care.
definitions.BOND: Evidence of a long-term debt, by which the bond issuer (the borrower) is obliged to pay interest when due, and repay the principal at maturity, as specified on the face of the bond certificate.
definitions.TRUST: Confidence in or reliance on some person or quality.
definitions.LEGACY: Money or property bequeathed to someone in a will.
definitions.GENERATION: The fact of creating something, or bringing something into being; production, creation.
definitions.ROOTS: The part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water and nutrients, and in some plants is able to perform vegetative reproduction.
definitions.HERITAGE: An inheritance; property that may be inherited.
definitions.TRADITION: A part of culture that is passed from person to person or generation to generation, possibly differing in detail from family to family, such as the way to celebrate holidays.
definitions.MEMORY: The ability of the brain to record information or impressions with the facility of recalling them later at will.
definitions.REUNION: The process or act of reuniting.
definitions.GATHERING: A meeting or get-together; a party or social function.
definitions.DINNER: A midday meal (in a context in which the evening meal is called supper or tea).
definitions.HOLIDAY: A day on which a festival, religious event, or national celebration is traditionally observed.
definitions.BIRTHDAY: The anniversary of the day on which someone is born.
definitions.WEDDING: To perform the marriage ceremony for; to join in matrimony.
definitions.ANNIVERSARY: A day that is an exact number of years (to the day) since a given significant event occurred.
definitions.CELEBRATION: The formal performance of a solemn rite, such as Christian sacrament.
definitions.GODCHILD: A child whose baptism is sponsored by a godparent.
definitions.GODFATHER: A man present at the christening of a baby who promises to help raise the child in a Christian manner; a male godparent who sponsors the baptism of a child.
definitions.GODMOTHER: A woman present at the christening of a baby who promises to help raise the child in a Christian manner; a female godparent who sponsors the baptism of a child.
definitions.STEPCHILD: The child of one's spouse but not one's own.
definitions.ADOPTED: To take by choice into relationship (a child, heir, friend, citizen, etc.).
definitions.TWINS: Either of two people (or, less commonly, animals) who shared the same uterus at the same time; one who was born at the same birth as a sibling.
definitions.PROGENY: Offspring or descendants considered as a group.
definitions.KINDRED: (often plurale tantum) Distant and close relatives, collectively.

definitions.ROSE: A beautiful flower of the genus Rosa, typically with thorns and sweet fragrance.
definitions.LILY: A large, bell-shaped flower growing from a bulb.
definitions.DAISY: A flower with white petals and a yellow center.
definitions.POPPY: Any plant of the genus Papaver or the family Papaveraceae, with crumpled, often red, petals and a milky juice having narcotic properties.
definitions.LOTUS: An aquatic plant with large, beautiful flowers, representing purity.
definitions.PHLOX: Any flowering plant of the genus Phlox.
definitions.PEONY: A large, rounded flower with many layers of petals.
definitions.ASTER: Any of several plants of the genus Aster.
definitions.IRIS: A plant of the genus Iris, common in the northern hemisphere, and generally having attractive blooms (See Iris (plant)).
definitions.ORCHID: An exotic, highly evolved flower with colorful, three-petaled blooms.
definitions.VIOLET: A small, delicate purple or blue flower.
definitions.PANSY: A cultivated flowering plant, derived by hybridization within species Viola tricolor.
definitions.CROCUS: A perennial flowering plant (of the genus Crocus in the Iridaceae family).
definitions.AZALEA: A plant of the obsolete genus Azalea.
definitions.LUPINE: Any member of the genus Lupinus in the family Fabaceae.
definitions.ZINNIA: Any of several brightly coloured flowering plants, of the genus Zinnia, native to tropical America; old maid.
definitions.DAHLIA: Any plant of the genus Dahlia, tuberous perennial flowering plants native to Mexico.
definitions.PETUNIA: Any of the flowering plants of genus Petunia, of which most garden varieties are hybrids.
definitions.JASMINE: A sweet-scented white or yellow flower used in perfumes.
definitions.LILAC: A large shrub of the genus Syringa, especially Syringa vulgaris, bearing white, pale-pink or purple flowers.
definitions.HEATHER: An evergreen plant, Calluna vulgaris, with spiky leaves and small purple, pink, or white flowers.
definitions.CLOVER: A plant of the genus Trifolium with leaves usually divided into three (rarely four) leaflets and with white or red flowers.
definitions.YARROW: Any of several pungent Eurasian and North American herbs, of the genus Achillea, used in traditional herbal medicine.
definitions.MALLOW: Any of a group of flowering plants in several genera of the taxonomic family Malvaceae, especially of the genus Malva.
definitions.THISTLE: Any of several perennial composite plants, especially of genera Cirsium, Carduus, Cynara, or Onopordum, having prickly leaves and showy flower heads with prickly bracts.
definitions.NETTLE: Any plant whose foliage is covered with stinging, mildly poisonous hairs, causing an instant rash.
definitions.FERN: Any of a group of some twenty thousand species of vascular plants classified in the division Pteridophyta that lack seeds and reproduce by shedding spores to initiate an alternation of generations.
definitions.MOSS: Any of various small, green, seedless plants growing on the ground or on the surfaces of trees, stones, etc.
definitions.BLOOM: A blossom; the flower of a plant; an expanded bud.
definitions.PETAL: One of the component parts of the corolla of a flower.
definitions.LEAF: The usually green and flat organ that represents the most prominent feature of most vegetative plants.
definitions.BUD: A newly sprouted leaf or blossom that has not yet unfolded.
definitions.SEED: A fertilized and ripened ovule, containing an embryonic plant.
definitions.ROOT: The part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water and nutrients, and in some plants is able to perform vegetative reproduction.
definitions.SOIL: A mixture of mineral particles and organic material, used to support plant growth.
definitions.GARDEN: An outdoor area containing one or more types of plants, usually plants grown for food or ornamental purposes.
definitions.FLOWER: A colorful, conspicuous structure associated with angiosperms, frequently scented and attracting various insects, and which may or may not be used for sexual reproduction.
definitions.SPRING: To weaken, as a joint, ligament, or muscle, by sudden and excessive exertion, as by wrenching.
definitions.SUMMER: One of four seasons, traditionally the second, marked by the longest and typically hottest days of the year due to the inclination of the Earth and thermal lag.
definitions.NATURE: The physical world and everything in it, including plants, animals, and landscapes.
definitions.BRIGHT: An artist's brush used in oil and acrylic painting with a long ferrule and a flat, somewhat tapering bristle head.
definitions.FRAGRANT: Sweet-smelling; having a pleasant (usually strong) scent or fragrance.
definitions.COLOR: The spectral composition of visible light.
definitions.BEAUTY: The quality of being (especially visually) attractive, pleasing, fine or good-looking; comeliness.
definitions.WILD: The undomesticated state of a wild animal.
definitions.FIELD: A land area free of woodland, cities, and towns; open country.
definitions.SUNFLOWER: A tall plant with a large, golden-yellow flower head that turns toward the sun.
definitions.MARIGOLD: (genericised brand name, usually plural, sometimes with capital) A rubber glove, especially one for use in household cleaning.
definitions.LAVENDER: A soothing purple flower known for its calming aroma.
definitions.BEGONIA: Any plant of the large genus of Begonia.
definitions.CAMELLIA: Any plant of the genus Camellia, shrubs and small trees native to Asia; Camellia japonica is the most popular as a garden plant; Camellia sinensis is the tea plant.
definitions.GARDENIA: Any of various tropical evergreen small trees or shrubs, of the genus Gardenia, having glossy leaves and white flowers.
definitions.HIBISCUS: A flower of the genus Hibiscus, especially Hibiscus syriacus, found in tropical to temperate regions, of some species used for making infusions/tea.
definitions.HYACINTH: Any bulbous plant of the genus Hyacinthus, native to the Mediterranean and South Africa.
definitions.MAGNOLIA: A tree or shrub in any species of the genus Magnolia, many with large flowers and simple leaves.
definitions.NARCISSUS: Any of several bulbous flowering plants, of the genus Narcissus, having white or yellow cup- or trumpet-shaped flowers, notably the daffodil.
definitions.OLEANDER: Nerium oleander, a notoriously poisonous shrub in the dogbane family, Apocynaceae, but nonetheless widely grown as an ornamental, having leathery lance-shaped leaves and deep rose-colored or white flowers.
definitions.PRIMROSE: A flowering plant of the genus Primula.
definitions.SNAPDRAGON: Any plant of the genus Antirrhinum, with showy yellow, white or red flowers.
definitions.VERBENA: Verbena, a genus of herbaceous plants of which several species are extensively cultivated for the great beauty of their flowers; vervain.
definitions.WISTERIA: Any of several woody climbing vines, of the genus Wisteria, native to the East Asian countries of China, Korea, and Japan and the eastern United States.
definitions.ANEMONE: Any plant of the genus Anemone, of the Ranunculaceae (or buttercup) family, such as the windflower.
definitions.BUTTERCUP: Any of many herbs, of the genus Ranunculus, having yellow flowers; the crowfoot.
definitions.CHRYSANTHEMUM: Any of many flowering perennial plants, of the genus Chrysanthemum, native to China, that have showy radiate heads.
definitions.FOXGLOVE: Digitalis, a genus of about 20 species of herbaceous biennials native to the Old World, certain of which are prized for their showy flowers.
definitions.GERANIUM: Any flowering plant of the genus Geranium, the cranesbills, of family Geraniaceae.
definitions.HOLLYHOCK: Any of several flowering plants of the genus Alcea in the Malvaceae family.
definitions.IMPATIENS: Any of various ornamental plants of the genus Impatiens.
definitions.LARKSPUR: Any plant of the genera Delphinium or Consolida.
definitions.NASTURTIUM: The popular name of any of the plants in the Tropaeolum genus of flowering plants native to south and central America.
definitions.PERIWINKLE: Any of several evergreen plants of the genus Vinca with blue or white flowers.
definitions.SWEETPEA: A flowering plant, Lathyrus odoratus, grown for its bright colours and sweet fragrance.
definitions.WALLFLOWER: Any of several short-lived herbs or shrubs of the Erysimum genus with bright yellow to red flowers.
definitions.WATERLILY: Any of various members of the Nymphaeaceae family that are tuberous plants, rooted in soil with leaves (lily pads) and flowers floating on the water surface.
definitions.BLUEBELL: Various flowering plants with blue, usually pendulous, flowers.
definitions.COLUMBINE: Any plant of the genus Aquilegia, having distinctive bell-shaped flowers with spurs on each petal.
definitions.CORNFLOWER: A small annual plant in the family Asteraceae, Centaurea cyanus, usually with bushy blue flowers which grows natively in European cornfields (i.e. wheatfields).
definitions.COWSLIP: A low-growing plant, Primula veris, with yellow flowers.
definitions.EDELWEISS: A European perennial alpine plant, Leontopodium alpinum, with downy leaves and small white flower heads in a dense cluster.
definitions.GOLDENROD: Any tall-stemmed plant principally from genus Solidago (also Oligoneuron), usually with clusters of small yellow flowers.
definitions.HONEYSUCKLE: Any of the many species of arching shrubs and climbing vines of the genus Lonicera in the Caprifoliaceae family, many with sweet smelling, bell shaped flowers.
definitions.MISTLETOE: Any of several hemiparasitic evergreen plants of the order Santalales with white berries that grow in the crowns of apple trees, oaks, and other trees, such as the European mistletoe (Viscum album) and American mistletoe or eastern mistletoe (Phoradendron leucarpum).
definitions.NIGHTSHADE: Any of the poisonous plants belonging to the genus Solanum, especially black nightshade or woody nightshade.
definitions.PROTEA: Any of many South African flowering plants, of the genus Protea, having colourful cone-shaped flower heads.
definitions.POINSETTIA: A plant, Euphorbia pulcherrima, with rather small and insignificant flowers but large brightly coloured leaves.
definitions.SNOWDROP: Any of the 20 species of the genus Galanthus of the Amaryllidaceae, bulbous flowering plants, bearing a solitary, pendulous, white, bell-shaped flower that appears, depending on species, between autumn and late winter or early spring, all native to temperate Eurasia.
definitions.VALERIAN: A hardy perennial flowering plant, Valeriana officinalis, with heads of sweetly scented pink or white flowers.
definitions.VERONICA: The image of Jesus's face believed to have been made on the cloth with which St Veronica wiped his face as he went to be crucified.
definitions.WINDFLOWER: An early spring flowering species of the family Ranunculaceae, Anemone nemorosa.
definitions.YUCCA: Any of several evergreen plants of the genus Yucca, having long, pointed, and rigid leaves at the top of a woody stem, and bearing a large panicle of showy white blossoms.

definitions.BREAD: A foodstuff made by baking dough made from cereals.
definitions.MILK: A white liquid produced by the mammary glands of female mammals to nourish their young.
definitions.EGGS: An approximately spherical or ellipsoidal body produced by birds, reptiles, insects and other animals, housing the embryo during its development.
definitions.RICE: Cereal plants, Oryza sativa of the grass family whose seeds are used as food.
definitions.MEAT: The flesh (muscle tissue) of an animal used as food.
definitions.FISH: A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water, moving with the help of fins and breathing with gills.
definitions.FRUIT: (often in the plural) In general, a product of plant growth useful to man or animals.
definitions.CAKE: A rich, sweet dessert food, typically made of flour, sugar and eggs and baked in an oven, and often covered in icing.
definitions.PIE: A type of pastry that consists of an outer crust and a filling.
definitions.SOUP: Any of various dishes commonly made by combining liquids, such as water or stock with other ingredients, such as meat and vegetables, that contribute flavor and texture.
definitions.APPLE: A common, round fruit produced by the tree Malus domestica, cultivated in temperate climates.
definitions.PEAR: An edible fruit produced by the pear tree, similar to an apple but elongated towards the stem.
definitions.BANANA: An elongated curved tropical fruit that grows in bunches and has a creamy flesh and a smooth skin.
definitions.GRAPE: A small, round, smooth-skinned edible fruit, usually purple, red, or green, that grows in bunches on vines of genus Vitis.
definitions.PEACH: A tree (Prunus persica), native to China and now widely cultivated throughout temperate regions, having pink flowers and edible fruit.
definitions.LIME: Any inorganic material containing calcium, usually calcium oxide (quicklime) or calcium hydroxide (slaked lime).
definitions.SEED: A fertilized and ripened ovule, containing an embryonic plant.
definitions.CORN: The main cereal plant grown for its grain in a given region, such as oats in parts of Scotland and Ireland, and wheat or barley in England and Wales.
definitions.PEA: A plant, Pisum sativum, member of the legume (Fabaceae) family.
definitions.BEAN: A reusable software component written in Java.
definitions.ONION: A monocotyledonous plant (Allium cepa), allied to garlic, used as vegetable and spice.
definitions.POTATO: The tuber of a plant, Solanum tuberosum, eaten as a starchy vegetable, particularly in the Americas and Europe; this plant.
definitions.CARROT: A vegetable with a nutritious, juicy, sweet root that is often orange in colour, Daucus carota, especially the subspecies sativus in the family Apiaceae.
definitions.TOMATO: A widely cultivated plant, Solanum lycopersicum, having edible fruit.
definitions.SALAD: A food made primarily of a mixture of raw or cold ingredients, typically vegetables, usually served with a dressing such as vinegar or mayonnaise.
definitions.SALT: A common substance, chemically consisting mainly of sodium chloride (NaCl), used extensively as a condiment and preservative.
definitions.SPICE: Aromatic or pungent plant matter (usually dried) used to season or flavour food.
definitions.SUGAR: Sucrose in the form of small crystals, obtained from sugar cane or sugar beet and used to sweeten food and drink.
definitions.HONEY: A viscous, sweet fluid produced from plant nectar by bees.
definitions.SWEET: The basic taste sensation induced by sugar.
definitions.SOUR: The sensation of a sour taste.
definitions.BITTER: (usually in the plural bitters) A liquid or powder, made from bitter herbs, used in mixed drinks or as a tonic.
definitions.TASTY: Having a pleasant or satisfying flavor; delicious.
definitions.FRESH: A rush of water, along a river or onto the land; a flood.
definitions.HOT: (with up) To heat; to make or become hot.
definitions.COLD: (of a thing) Having a low temperature.
definitions.FOOD: Any solid substance that can be consumed by living organisms, especially by eating, in order to sustain life.
definitions.LUNCH: A light meal usually eaten around midday, notably when not as main meal of the day.
definitions.DINNER: A midday meal (in a context in which the evening meal is called supper or tea).
definitions.MEAL: Food that is prepared and eaten, usually at a specific time, and usually in a comparatively large quantity (as opposed to a snack).
definitions.CHEESE: A dairy product made from curdled or cultured milk.
definitions.BUTTER: A soft, fatty foodstuff made by churning the cream of milk (generally cow's milk).
definitions.CREAM: The butterfat/milkfat part of milk which rises to the top; this part when separated from the remainder.
definitions.YOGURT: A milk-based product stiffened by a bacterium-aided curdling process, and sometimes mixed with fruit or other flavoring.
definitions.PASTA: Dough made from wheat and water and sometimes mixed with egg and formed into various shapes; often sold in dried form and typically boiled for eating.
definitions.PIZZA: A baked Italian dish of a thinly rolled bread dough crust typically topped before baking with tomato sauce, cheese and other ingredients such as meat, vegetables or fruit.
definitions.STEAK: Beefsteak, a slice of beef, broiled or cut for broiling.
definitions.CHICKEN: A domestic fowl, Gallus gallus, especially when young.
definitions.BACON: Cured meat from the sides, belly or back of a pig.
definitions.SAUSAGE: A food made of ground meat (or meat substitute) and seasoning, packed in a section of the animal's intestine, or in a similarly cylindrical shaped synthetic casing; a length of this food.
definitions.SHRIMP: Any of many swimming, often edible crustaceans, chiefly of the infraorder Caridea or the suborder Dendrobranchiata, with slender legs, long whiskers and a long abdomen.
definitions.CRAB: A crustacean of the infraorder Brachyura, having five pairs of legs, the foremost of which are in the form of claws, and a carapace.
definitions.LOBSTER: A crustacean of the Nephropidae family, dark green or blue-black in colour turning bright red when cooked, with a hard shell and claws, which is used as a seafood.
definitions.SALMON: One of several species of fish, typically of the Salmoninae subfamily, brownish above with silvery sides and delicate pinkish-orange flesh; they ascend rivers to spawn.
definitions.TUNA: Any of several species of fish of the genus Thunnus in the family Scombridae.
definitions.SPINACH: A particular edible plant, Spinacia oleracea, or its leaves.
definitions.BROCCOLI: A plant, Brassica oleracea var. italica, of the cabbage family, Brassicaceae; especially, the tree-shaped flower and stalk that are eaten as a vegetable.
definitions.CABBAGE: An edible plant (Brassica oleracea var. capitata) having a head of green leaves.
definitions.LETTUCE: An edible plant, Lactuca sativa and its close relatives, having a head of green and/or purple leaves.
definitions.CUCUMBER: A vine in the gourd family, Cucumis sativus.
definitions.PEPPER: A plant of the family Piperaceae.
definitions.GARLIC: A plant, Allium sativum, related to the onion, having a pungent bulb much used in cooking.
definitions.GINGER: The pungent aromatic rhizome of a tropical Asian herb, Zingiber officinale, used as a spice and as a stimulant and acarminative.
definitions.PARSLEY: A bright green, biennial herb, Petroselinum crispum, having many cultivars.
definitions.MINT: A building or institution where money (originally, only coins) is produced under government licence.
definitions.ROSEMARY: A shrub, Rosmarinus officinalis, that originates from Europe and Asia Minor and produces a fragrant herb used in cooking and perfumes.
definitions.THYME: Any plant of the labiate genus Thymus, such as the garden thyme, Thymus vulgaris, a warm, pungent aromatic, that is much used to give a relish to seasoning and soups.
definitions.OREGANO: A herb of the mint family, Origanum vulgare, having aromatic leaves.
definitions.CINNAMON: A small evergreen tree native to Sri Lanka and southern India, Cinnamomum verum or Cinnamomum zeylanicum, belonging to the family Lauraceae.
definitions.VANILLA: Any tropical, climbing orchid of the genus Vanilla (especially Vanilla planifolia), bearing podlike fruit yielding an extract used in flavoring food or in perfumes.
definitions.CHOCOLATE: A food made from ground roasted cocoa beans.
definitions.CANDY: Edible, sweet-tasting confectionery containing sugar, or sometimes artificial sweeteners, and often flavored with fruit, chocolate, nuts, herbs and spices, or artificial flavors.
definitions.COOKIE: A small, flat, baked good which is either crisp or soft but firm.
definitions.DONUT: A deep-fried piece of dough or batter, commonly made in a toroidal or ellipsoidal shape, and mixed with various sweeteners and flavors, sometimes filled with jelly, custard or cream.
definitions.MUFFIN: A type of flattish bun, usually cut in two horizontally, toasted and spread with butter, etc, before being eaten.
definitions.PANCAKE: A thin batter cake fried in a pan or on a griddle in oil or butter.
definitions.WAFFLE: A flat pastry pressed with a grid pattern.
definitions.CEREAL: A type of grass (such as wheat, rice or oats) cultivated for its edible grains.
definitions.OATMEAL: Meal made from rolled or round oats.
definitions.GRANOLA: A breakfast and snack food consisting of loose, crispy pellets made of nuts, rolled oats, honey and other natural ingredients.
definitions.BAGEL: A toroidal bread roll that is boiled before it is baked.
definitions.SANDWICH: A dish or foodstuff where two or more slices of bread serve as the wrapper or container of some other food.
definitions.WRAP: To enclose (an object) completely in any flexible, thin material such as fabric or paper.
definitions.BURRITO: A Mexican dish consisting of a flour tortilla wrapped around a filling of meat and/or beans, cheese etc.
definitions.SUSHI: A Japanese dish made of small portions of sticky white rice flavored with vinegar, usually wrapped in seaweed and filled or topped with fish, vegetables or meat.
definitions.RAMEN: Soup noodles of wheat, with various ingredients (Japanese style).
definitions.NOODLE: (usually in the plural) a string or strip of pasta.
definitions.CURRY: One of a family of dishes originating from South Asian cuisine, flavoured by a spiced sauce.
definitions.CHILI: The pungent, spicy fresh or dried fruit of any of several cultivated varieties of capsicum peppers, used in cooking.
definitions.QUICHE: A pie made primarily of eggs and cream in a pastry crust.

definitions.ART: The conscious production or arrangement of sounds, colours, forms, movements, or other elements in a manner that affects the senses and emotions, usually specifically the production of the beautiful in a graphic or plastic medium.
definitions.DRAW: The result of a contest that neither side has won; a tie.
definitions.PAINT: A substance that is applied as a liquid or paste, and dries into a solid coating that protects or adds color/colour to an object or surface to which it has been applied.
definitions.READ: A reading or an act of reading, especially an actor's part of a play.
definitions.WRITE: The act or style of writing.
definitions.SING: A gathering at which people sing songs.
definitions.DANCE: A sequence of rhythmic steps or movements usually performed to music, for pleasure or as a form of social interaction.
definitions.BAKE: The act of cooking food by baking.
definitions.SEW: To use a needle to pass thread repeatedly through (pieces of fabric) in order to join them together.
definitions.SWIM: An act or instance of swimming.
definitions.BIKE: A vehicle that has two wheels, one behind the other, a steering handle, and a saddle seat or seats and is usually propelled by the action of a rider’s feet upon pedals.
definitions.CAMP: An outdoor place acting as temporary accommodation in tents or other temporary structures.
definitions.FISH: A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water, moving with the help of fins and breathing with gills.
definitions.PLAY: Activity for amusement only, especially among the young.
definitions.GARDEN: An outdoor area containing one or more types of plants, usually plants grown for food or ornamental purposes.
definitions.TRAVEL: The act of traveling; passage from place to place.
definitions.MOVIE: A recorded sequence of images displayed on a screen at a rate sufficiently fast to create the appearance of motion.
definitions.MUSIC: A series of sounds organized in time, employing melody, harmony, tempo etc. usually to convey a mood.
definitions.BAND: A strip of material used for strengthening or coupling.
definitions.DRUM: A percussive musical instrument spanned with a thin covering on at least one end for striking, forming an acoustic chamber, affecting what materials are used to make it; a membranophone.
definitions.PIANO: A percussive keyboard musical instrument, usually ranging over seven octaves, with white and black colored keys, played by pressing these keys, causing hammers to strike strings.
definitions.GUITAR: A stringed musical instrument, of European origin, usually with a fretted fingerboard and six strings, played with the fingers or a plectrum (guitar pick).
definitions.CHESS: A board game for two players with each beginning with sixteen chess pieces moving according to fixed rules across a chessboard with the objective to checkmate the opposing king.
definitions.DICE: Gaming with one or more dice.
definitions.PUZZLE: Anything that is difficult to understand or make sense of.
definitions.HOBBY: An activity that one enjoys doing in one's spare time.
definitions.BUILD: The physique of a human body; constitution or structure of a human body.
definitions.SHOP: An establishment that sells goods or services to the public.
definitions.STUDY: (usually academic) To review materials already learned in order to make sure one does not forget them, usually in preparation for an examination.
definitions.TEACH: To show (someone) the way; to guide, conduct; to point, indicate.
definitions.HELP: Action given to provide assistance; aid.
definitions.SERVE: An act of putting the ball or shuttlecock in play in various games.
definitions.LIVE: To be alive; to have life.
definitions.GROW: To become larger, to increase in magnitude.
definitions.BE: A prefix, originally the same word as by.
definitions.SKETCH: A rapidly executed freehand drawing that is not intended as a finished work, often consisting of a multitude of overlapping lines.
definitions.POTTERY: Fired ceramic wares that contain clay when formed.
definitions.WEAVE: A type or way of weaving.
definitions.QUILT: A bed covering consisting of two layers of fabric stitched together, with insulation between, often having a decorative design.
definitions.SCRAPBOOK: A book, similar to a notebook or journal, in which personal or family memorabilia and photos are collected and arranged.
definitions.JOURNAL: A diary or daily record of a person, organization, vessel etc.; daybook.
definitions.POETRY: Literature composed in verse or language exhibiting conscious attention to patterns and rhythm.
definitions.MAGIC: The application of rituals or actions, especially those based on occult knowledge, to subdue or manipulate natural or supernatural beings and forces in order to have some benefit from them.
definitions.CIRCUS: A traveling company of performers that may include acrobats, clowns, trained animals, and other novelty acts, that gives shows usually in a circular tent.
definitions.YOGA: Any of several Hindu or Buddhist disciplines aimed at training the consciousness for a state of perfect spiritual insight and tranquillity.
definitions.PILATES: A physical fitness system developed in the early 20th century by Joseph Pilates.
definitions.KARATE: An Okinawan martial art involving primarily punching and kicking, but additionally, advanced throws, arm bars, grappling and all means of fighting.
definitions.TENNIS: A sport played by two players (or four in doubles), who alternately strike the ball over a net using racquets.
definitions.GOLF: A ball game played by individuals competing against one another in which the object is to hit a ball into each of a series of (usually 18 or nine) holes in the minimum number of strokes.
definitions.HOCKEY: Ice hockey, a game on ice in which two teams of six players skate and try to score by shooting a puck into the opposing team's net, using their sticks.
definitions.SKATING: To move along a surface (ice or ground) using skates.
definitions.SURFING: To ride a wave, usually on a surfboard.
definitions.SAILING: To be impelled or driven forward by the action of wind upon sails, as a ship on water.
definitions.ROWING: To propel (a boat or other craft) over water using oars.
definitions.DRIVING: To provide an impetus for motion or other physical change, to move an object by means of the provision of force thereto.
definitions.RACING: To take part in a race (in the sense of a contest).
definitions.RIDING: To transport oneself by sitting on and directing a horse, later also a bicycle etc.
definitions.WALKING: To move on the feet by alternately setting each foot (or pair or group of feet, in the case of animals with four or more feet) forward, with at least one foot on the ground at all times.
definitions.STARGAZE: To look at the stars at night.
definitions.COINS: (money) A piece of currency, usually metallic and in the shape of a disc, but sometimes polygonal, or with a hole in the middle.
definitions.STAMPS: An act of stamping the foot, paw or hoof.
definitions.ANTIQUE: A grotesque representation of a figure; a gargoyle.
definitions.ROASTING: To cook food by heating in an oven or over a fire without covering, resulting in a crisp, possibly even slightly charred appearance.
definitions.BREWING: To make tea or coffee by mixing tea leaves or coffee beans with hot water.
definitions.TASTING: A small amount of food or drink.
definitions.FARMING: To work on a farm, especially in the growing and harvesting of crops.
definitions.ROBOTS: A machine built to carry out some complex task or group of tasks by physically moving, especially one which can be programmed.
definitions.DRONES: A male ant, bee or wasp, which does not work but can fertilize the queen bee.
definitions.MODELING: To display for others to see, especially in regard to wearing clothing while performing the role of a fashion model.
definitions.RIDDLES: A verbal puzzle, mystery, or other problem of an intellectual nature.
definitions.ORIGAMI: The Japanese art of paper folding.
definitions.CALLIGRAPHY: The art or practice of writing letters and words in a decorative style; the letters and words so written.
definitions.JEWELRY: Collectively, personal ornamentation such as rings, necklaces, brooches and bracelets, made of precious metals and sometimes set with gemstones.

definitions.HOUSE: A structure built or serving as an abode of human beings.
definitions.WALL: A rampart of earth, stones etc. built up for defensive purposes.
definitions.DOOR: A portal of entry into a building, room, or vehicle, consisting of a rigid plane movable on a hinge.
definitions.ROOF: The external covering at the top of a building.
definitions.FLOOR: The interior bottom or surface of a house or building; the supporting surface of a room.
definitions.STAIR: A single step in a staircase.
definitions.BATH: A tub or pool which is used for bathing: bathtub.
definitions.BED: A piece of furniture, usually flat and soft, on which to rest or sleep.
definitions.DESK: A table, frame, or case, in past centuries usually with a sloping top but now usually with a flat top, for the use of writers and readers.
definitions.CHAIR: An item of furniture used to sit on or in, comprising a seat, legs, back, and sometimes arm rests, for use by one person.
definitions.TABLE: Furniture with a top surface to accommodate a variety of uses.
definitions.COUCH: Couch grass, a species of persistent grass, Elymus repens, usually considered a weed.
definitions.LAMP: A device that generates heat, light or other radiation.
definitions.RUG: A partial covering for a floor.
definitions.MAT: A flat piece of coarse material used for wiping one’s feet, or as a decorative or protective floor covering.
definitions.BOX: Senses relating to a three-dimensional object or space.
definitions.BIN: A box, frame, crib, or enclosed place, used as a storage container.
definitions.CUP: A concave vessel for drinking from, usually made of opaque material (as opposed to a glass) and with a handle.
definitions.DISH: A vessel such as a plate for holding or serving food, often flat with a depressed region in the middle.
definitions.BOWL: A roughly hemispherical container used to hold, mix or present food, such as salad, fruit or soup, or other items.
definitions.FORK: A pronged tool having a long straight handle, used for digging, lifting, throwing etc.
definitions.KNIFE: A utensil or a tool designed for cutting, consisting of a flat piece of hard material, usually steel or other metal (the blade), usually sharpened on one edge, attached to a handle.
definitions.SPOON: An implement for eating or serving; a scooped utensil whose long handle is straight, in contrast to a ladle.
definitions.POT: A flat-bottomed vessel (usually metal) used for cooking food.
definitions.PAN: A wide, flat receptacle used around the house, especially for cooking.
definitions.OVEN: A chamber used for baking or heating.
definitions.SINK: A basin used for holding water for washing.
definitions.TUB: A flat-bottomed vessel, of width similar to or greater than its height, used for storing or packing things, or for washing things in.
definitions.SHOWER: A brief fall of precipitation (spell of rain, or a similar fall of snow, sleet, or cascade).
definitions.SOAP: A substance able to mix with both oil and water, used for cleaning, often in the form of a solid bar or in liquid form, derived from fats or made synthetically.
definitions.TOWEL: A cloth used for wiping, especially one used for drying anything wet, as a person after a bath.
definitions.COMB: A toothed implement for grooming the hair or (formerly) for keeping it in place.
definitions.BRUSH: An implement consisting of multiple more or less flexible bristles or other filaments attached to a handle, used for any of various purposes including cleaning, painting, and arranging hair.
definitions.MIRROR: A smooth surface, usually made of glass with reflective material painted on the underside, that reflects light so as to give an image of what is in front of it.
definitions.CLOCK: An instrument used to measure or keep track of time.
definitions.KEY: An object designed to open and close a lock.
definitions.LOCK: Something used for fastening, which can only be opened with a key or combination.
definitions.BOOK: A collection of sheets of paper bound together to hinge at one edge, containing printed or written material, pictures, etc.
definitions.PEN: An enclosure (enclosed area) used to contain domesticated animals, especially sheep or cattle.
definitions.PAPER: A sheet material used for writing on or printing on (or as a non-waterproof container), usually made by draining cellulose fibres from a suspension in water.
definitions.PHONE: A device for transmitting conversations and other sounds in real time across distances, now often a small portable unit also capable of running software etc.
definitions.TOY: Something to play with, especially as intended for use by a child.
definitions.CLOTH: A woven fabric such as used in dressing, decorating, cleaning or other practical use.
definitions.SHOE: A protective covering for the foot, with a bottom part composed of thick leather or plastic sole and often a thicker heel, and a softer upper part made of leather or synthetic material.
definitions.SOCK: A knitted or woven covering for the foot.
definitions.HAT: A covering for the head, often in the approximate form of a cone or a cylinder closed at its top end, and sometimes having a brim and other decoration.
definitions.BAG: A flexible container made of cloth, paper, plastic, etc.
definitions.KITCHEN: A room or area for preparing food.
definitions.PANTRY: A small room, closet, or cabinet usually located in or near the kitchen, dedicated to shelf-stable food storage and/or storing kitchenware, like a larder, but smaller.
definitions.FREEZER: An appliance or room used to store food or other perishable items at temperatures below 0° Celsius (32° Fahrenheit).
definitions.TOASTER: One who toasts (cooks lightly by browning).
definitions.BLENDER: A machine outfitted with sharp blades, for mashing, crushing or liquefying food ingredients.
definitions.MIXER: One who, or a device that, mixes or merges things together.
definitions.KETTLE: A vessel for boiling a liquid or cooking food, usually metal and equipped with a lid.
definitions.COFFEE: A beverage made by infusing the beans of the coffee plant in hot water.
definitions.TEA: A drug smoked or ingested for euphoric effect, cannabis.
definitions.BEDROOM: A room in a house where a bed is kept for sleeping.
definitions.PILLOW: A soft cushion used to support the head in bed.
definitions.BLANKET: A heavy, loosely woven fabric, usually large and woollen, used for warmth while sleeping or resting.
definitions.SHEET: A thin bed cloth used as a covering for a mattress or as a layer over the sleeper.
definitions.CLOSET: Any private area, (particularly) bowers in the open air.
definitions.DRAWER: An open-topped box that can be slid in and out of the cabinet that contains it, used for storing clothing or other articles.
definitions.HANGER: One who hangs, or causes to be hanged; a hangman, paper hanger, etc.
definitions.CABINET: A storage closet either separate from, or built into, a wall.
definitions.SHELF: A flat, rigid structure, fixed at right angles to a wall or forming a part of a cabinet, desk etc., and used to support, store or display objects.
definitions.FRAME: The structural elements of a building or other constructed object.
definitions.WASHER: Something that washes; especially an appliance such as a washing machine or dishwasher.
definitions.DRYER: One who, or that which, dries; a desiccative.
definitions.IRON: A common, inexpensive metal, silvery grey when untarnished, that rusts, is attracted by magnets, and is used in making steel.
definitions.BASKET: A lightweight container, generally round, open at the top, and tapering toward the bottom.
definitions.BROOM: A domestic utensil with fibers bound together at the end of a long handle, used for sweeping.
definitions.VACUUM: A region of space that contains no matter.
definitions.MOP: An implement for washing floors, or the like, made of a piece of cloth, or a collection of thrums, or coarse yarn, fastened to a handle.
definitions.TRASH: Useless things to be discarded; rubbish; refuse.
definitions.WINDOW: The inedible parts of a grain-producing plant.
definitions.BLIND: A covering for a window to keep out light.
definitions.CURTAIN: A piece of cloth covering a window, bed, etc. to offer privacy and keep out light.
definitions.SHUTTER: One who shuts or closes something.
definitions.PORCH: A covered and enclosed entrance to a building, whether taken from the interior, and forming a sort of vestibule within the main wall, or projecting without and with a separate roof.
definitions.PATIO: A paved outside area, adjoining a house, used for dining or recreation.
definitions.GARAGE: A building (or section of a building) used to store a car or cars, tools and other miscellaneous items.
definitions.ATTIC: The space, often unfinished and with sloped walls, directly below the roof in the uppermost part of a house or other building, generally used for storage or habitation.
definitions.CELLAR: An enclosed underground space, often under a building, used for storage or shelter.
definitions.BASEMENT: A floor of a building below ground level.
definitions.GARDEN: An outdoor area containing one or more types of plants, usually plants grown for food or ornamental purposes.
definitions.FENCE: A thin artificial barrier that separates two pieces of land or a house perimeter.
definitions.GATE: A doorlike structure outside a house.
definitions.YARD: A small, usually uncultivated area adjoining or (now especially) within the precincts of a house or other building.
definitions.DRIVE: Motivation to do or achieve something; ability coupled with ambition.
definitions.CHIMNEY: A vertical tube or hollow column used to emit environmentally polluting gaseous and solid matter (including but not limited to by-products of burning carbon or hydrocarbon based fuels); a flue.
definitions.HEATER: A device that produces and radiates heat, typically to raise the temperature of a room or building.
definitions.COOLER: Having a slightly low temperature; mildly or pleasantly cold.
definitions.REMOTE: An element of broadcast programming originating away from the station's or show's control room.

definitions.DRUM: A percussive musical instrument spanned with a thin covering on at least one end for striking, forming an acoustic chamber, affecting what materials are used to make it; a membranophone.
definitions.BELL: A percussive instrument made of metal or other hard material, typically but not always in the shape of an inverted cup with a flared rim, which resonates when struck.
definitions.HORN: A hard growth of keratin that protrudes from the top of the head of certain animals, usually paired.
definitions.HARP: A musical instrument consisting of a body and a curved neck, strung with strings of varying length that are stroked or plucked with the fingers and are vertical to the soundboard when viewed from the end of the body.
definitions.LUTE: A fretted stringed instrument of European origin, similar to the guitar, having a bowl-shaped body or soundbox; any of a wide variety of chordophones with a pear-shaped body and a neck whose upper surface is in the same plane as the soundboard, with strings along the neck and parallel to the soundboard.
definitions.PIPE: Meanings relating to a wind instrument.
definitions.REED: Any of various types of tall stiff perennial grass-like plants growing together in groups near water.
definitions.SONG: A musical composition with lyrics for voice or voices, performed by singing.
definitions.BAND: A strip of material used for strengthening or coupling.
definitions.PIANO: A percussive keyboard musical instrument, usually ranging over seven octaves, with white and black colored keys, played by pressing these keys, causing hammers to strike strings.
definitions.ORGAN: A larger part of an organism, composed of tissues that perform similar functions.
definitions.FLUTE: A woodwind instrument consisting of a tube with a row of holes that produce sound through vibrations caused by air blown across the edge of the holes, often tuned by plugging one or more holes with a finger; the Western concert flute, a transverse side-blown flute of European origin.
definitions.BANJO: A stringed musical instrument (chordophone), usually with a round body, a membrane-like soundboard and a fretted neck, played by plucking or strumming the strings.
definitions.CELLO: A large stringed instrument of the violin family with four strings, tuned from lowest to highest C-G-D-A, and played with a bow, also possessing an endpin to support the instrument's weight.
definitions.VIOLA: A stringed instrument of the violin family, somewhat larger than a violin, played under the chin, and having a deeper tone.
definitions.TUBA: A large brass musical instrument, usually in the bass range, played through a vibration of the lips upon the mouthpiece and fingering of the keys.
definitions.OBOE: A soprano and melody wind instrument in the modern orchestra and wind ensemble.
definitions.GONG: A percussion instrument consisting of a metal disk that emits a sonorous sound when struck with a soft hammer.
definitions.LYRE: An ancient stringed musical instrument (a yoke lute chordophone) of Greek origin, consisting of two arms extending from a body to a crossbar (a yoke), and strings, parallel to the soundboard, connecting the body to the yoke.
definitions.GUITAR: A stringed musical instrument, of European origin, usually with a fretted fingerboard and six strings, played with the fingers or a plectrum (guitar pick).
definitions.FIDDLE: Any of various bowed string instruments, often a violin when played in any of various traditional styles, as opposed to classical violin.
definitions.TRUMPET: A musical instrument of the brass family, generally tuned to the key of B-flat.
definitions.HARMONICA: A musical wind instrument with a series of holes for the player to blow into, each hole producing a different note.
definitions.CLARINET: A woodwind musical instrument that has a distinctive liquid tone whose characteristics vary among its three registers: chalumeau (low), clarion (medium), and altissimo (high).
definitions.SAXOPHONE: A single-reed instrument musical instrument of the woodwind family, usually made of brass and with a distinctive loop bringing the bell upwards.
definitions.TROMBONE: A musical instrument in the brass family, having a cylindrical bore, and usually a sliding tube (but sometimes piston valves, and rarely both).
definitions.XYLOPHONE: Any musical instrument (percussion idiophone) made of wooden slats graduated so as to make the sounds of the scale when struck with a small drumstick-like mallet; the standard Western concert xylophone or one of its derivatives.
definitions.TAMBOURINE: A percussion instrument consisting of a small, usually wooden, hoop closed on one side with a drum frame and featuring jingling metal disks on the tread; it is most often held in the hand and shaken rhythmically; by extension, any frame drum.
definitions.CYMBAL: A concave plate of brass or bronze that produces a sharp, ringing sound when struck: played either in pairs, by striking them together, or singly by striking with a drumstick or the like.
definitions.TRIANGLE: A polygon with three sides and three angles.
definitions.WHISTLE: A device designed to be placed in the mouth and blown, or driven by steam or some other mechanism, to make a whistling sound.
definitions.KEYBOARD: (etc.) A set of keys used to operate a typewriter, computer etc.
definitions.BASSOON: A musical instrument in the woodwind family, having a double reed and playing in the tenor and bass ranges.
definitions.PICCOLO: An instrument similar to a flute, but smaller, and playing an octave higher.
definitions.MANDOLIN: A stringed instrument and a member of the lute family, having eight strings in four courses, frequently tuned as a violin, and with either a bowl-shaped back or a flat back.
definitions.ACCORDION: A small, portable, keyed wind instrument, whose tones are generated by play of the wind from a squeezed bellows upon free metallic reeds.
definitions.CONCERTINA: A musical instrument, like the various accordions, that is a member of the free-reed family of musical instruments, typically having buttons on both ends.
definitions.DIDGERIDOO: A musical instrument endemic to the Top End of Australia, consisting of a long hollowed-out log, which, when blown into, produces a low, deep mesmerising drone with sweeping rhythms.
