definitions.THEREMIN: An electronic musical instrument that generates sound of varying pitch and volume depending on the proximity of the musician’s hands to two antennae mounted on the instrument.
definitions.SYNTHESIZER: An electronic instrument that creates its sounds with electronics and has a keyboard.
definitions.MARIMBA: A musical instrument similar to a xylophone but clearer in pitch.
definitions.GLOCKENSPIEL: A musical instrument of the percussion idiophone family of instruments; like the xylophone, it has tuned bars arranged like the keys on a piano, and is also smaller in size and higher in pitch.
definitions.CASTANETS: A percussion instrument (idiophone) of Spanish origin, consisting of a pair of concave shells joined on one edge by a string, held in the hand and used to produce clicking sounds; any hand-held percussion idiophone that can be played with the fingers, such as bones or spoons.
definitions.MARACAS: A Latin American percussion instrument consisting of a hollow-gourd rattle containing pebbles or beans and often played in pairs, as a rhythm instrument.
definitions.BONGOS: A striped bovine mammal found in Africa, Tragelaphus eurycerus.
definitions.CONGA: A tall, narrow, single-headed Cuban hand drum of African origin.
definitions.TIMPANI: The set of precision kettledrums in an orchestra.
definitions.TABLA: A pair of tuned hand drums, used in various musical genres of the Indian subcontinent, that are similar to bongos.
definitions.SITAR: A Hindustani/Indian classical stringed instrument, typically having a gourd as its resonating chamber.
definitions.KOTO: A Japanese stringed instrument having numerous strings, usually seven or thirteen, that are stretched over a convex wooden sounding board and are plucked with three plectra, worn on the thumb, index finger, and middle finger of one hand.
definitions.SHAMISEN: A kind of three-stringed Japanese fretless lute.
definitions.PIPA: A pear-shaped plucked lute from China.
definitions.BALALAIKA: A plucked stringed instrument with a triangular body, short neck and three strings, of Russian origin.
definitions.BOUZOUKI: A Greek long-necked plucked fretted lute having a sharp, metallic sound.
definitions.VIOLIN: A musical four-string instrument, generally played with a bow or by plucking the string, with the pitch set by pressing the strings at the appropriate place with the fingers; also any instrument of the violin family.
definitions.CORNET: A musical instrument of the brass family, slightly smaller than a trumpet, usually in the musical key of B-flat.
definitions.EUPHONIUM: A valved brass instrument, a sax horn, the tenor of the tuba family of instruments, having the appearance very similar to that of a tuba.
definitions.SHAWM: A mediaeval double-reed wind instrument with a conical wooden body.
definitions.SHAKUHACHI: A Japanese flute which is tuned to a pentatonic scale is end-blown like a recorder instead of being held transversely like the Western transverse flute.
definitions.OCARINA: A woodwind musical instrument that is closed at both sides to produce an enclosed space, and punctured with finger holes.
definitions.KALIMBA: A type of thumb piano, similar to a mbira.
definitions.MBIRA: A thumb piano, a musical instrument having a small sound box fitted with a row of tuned tabs that are plucked with the thumbs, originating among the Shona of southern Africa; any type of plucked lamellophone of the same type as the Shona instrument.
definitions.DJEMBE: A large, skin-covered drum played with the hands, used in West African and some fusion music.
definitions.ZITHER: A musical instrument consisting of a flat sounding box with numerous strings placed on a horizontal surface, played with a plectrum or fingertips.
definitions.AUTOHARP: A string instrument having a series of chord bars attached to dampers (muting bars) which mute all the strings other than those that form the desired chord.
definitions.DULCIMER: A stringed instrument, with strings stretched across a sounding board, usually trapezoidal.
definitions.PSALTERY: A zither-like musical instrument consisting of a soundboard with multiple strings, played by plucking the strings with the fingers or a plectrum.
definitions.LUR: A long natural blowing horn without finger holes, played by embouchure.
definitions.SACKBUT: A brass instrument from the Renaissance and Baroque Eras, and an ancestor of the modern trombone.
definitions.OPHICLEIDE: A keyed brass baritone bugle, now replaced by the tuba in orchestral music.
definitions.HELICON: A large tuba whose coils fit around the player's shoulders.
definitions.SOUSAPHONE: A valved brass instrument with the same length as a tuba, but shaped differently so that the bell is above the head, that the valves are situated directly in front of the musical instruments and a few inches above the waist, and that most of the weight rests on one shoulder.
definitions.HARPSICHORD: A musical instrument with a keyboard that produces sound through a mechanical process.
definitions.CLAVICHORD: An early keyboard instrument producing a soft sound by means of metal blades (called tangents) attached to the inner ends of the keys gently striking the strings.
definitions.SPINET: A short, compact harpsichord or piano.
definitions.CELESTA: A musical instrument consisting principally of a set of graduated steel plates struck with hammers that are activated by a keyboard.
definitions.VIBRAPHONE: A percussion instrument with a double row of tuned metal bars, each above the tubular resonator containing a motor-driven rotating vane, giving a vibrato effect.
definitions.CHIMES: A musical instrument producing a sound when struck, similar to a bell (e.g. a tubular metal bar) or actually a bell.
definitions.COWBELL: The lead cow in a herd.
definitions.GUIRO: A musical instrument, a shaker, made of a hollow gourd with parallel notches cut in one side, and played by rubbing a stick or scraper ("pua") along the notches to produce a ratchet-like sound.

definitions.TREE: Fast growing function based on Kruskal's tree theorem.
definitions.LEAF: The usually green and flat organ that represents the most prominent feature of most vegetative plants.
definitions.ROOT: The part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water and nutrients, and in some plants is able to perform vegetative reproduction.
definitions.BARK: The short, loud, explosive sound uttered by a dog, a fox, and some other animals.
definitions.WOOD: The substance making up the central part of the trunk and branches of a tree.
definitions.MOSS: Any of various small, green, seedless plants growing on the ground or on the surfaces of trees, stones, etc.
definitions.FERN: Any of a group of some twenty thousand species of vascular plants classified in the division Pteridophyta that lack seeds and reproduce by shedding spores to initiate an alternation of generations.
definitions.BUSH: A woody plant distinguished from a tree by its multiple stems and lower height, being usually less than six metres tall.
definitions.VINE: The climbing plant that produces grapes.
definitions.SAND: Rock that is ground more finely than gravel, but is not as fine as silt (more formally, see grain sizes chart), forming beaches and deserts and also used in construction.
definitions.CLAY: A mineral substance made up of small crystals of silica and alumina, that is ductile when moist.
definitions.SOIL: A mixture of mineral particles and organic material, used to support plant growth.
definitions.HILL: An elevated location smaller than a mountain.
definitions.CAVE: A large, naturally-occurring cavity formed underground or in the face of a cliff or a hillside.
definitions.GLEN: A secluded and narrow valley, especially one with a river running through it.
definitions.LAKE: A small stream of running water; a channel for water; a drain.
definitions.POND: An inland body of standing water, either natural or man-made, that is smaller than a lake.
definitions.POOL: A small and rather deep collection of (usually) fresh water, as one supplied by a spring, or occurring in the course of a stream; a reservoir for water.
definitions.RIVER: A large and often winding stream which drains a land mass, carrying water down from higher areas to a lower point, oftentimes ending in another body of water, such as an ocean or in an inland sea.
definitions.BROOK: To use; enjoy; have the full employment of.
definitions.CREEK: A small inlet or bay, often saltwater, narrower and extending farther into the land than a cove; a recess in the shore of the sea, or of a river; the inner part of a port that is used as a dock for small boats.
definitions.OCEAN: One of the large bodies of water separating the continents.
definitions.SEA: A large body of salt water.
definitions.WAVE: To move back and forth repeatedly and somewhat loosely.
definitions.TIDE: The periodic change of the sea level, particularly when caused by the gravitational influence of the sun and the moon.
definitions.RAIN: Condensed water falling from a cloud.
definitions.SNOW: The frozen, crystalline state of water that falls as precipitation.
definitions.HAIL: Balls or pieces of ice falling as precipitation, often in connection with a thunderstorm.
definitions.DEW: Any moisture from the atmosphere condensed by cool bodies upon their surfaces.
definitions.MIST: Water or other liquid finely suspended in air.
definitions.FOG: A thick cloud that forms near the ground; the obscurity of such a cloud.
definitions.WIND: Real or perceived movement of atmospheric air usually caused by convection or differences in air pressure.
definitions.STORM: Any disturbed state of the atmosphere, especially as affecting the earth's surface, and strongly implying destructive or unpleasant weather.
definitions.SUN: A star, especially when seen as the centre of any single solar system.
definitions.MOON: The Earth's moon Luna; the sole natural satellite of the Earth, represented in astronomy and astrology by ☾.
definitions.STAR: Any small luminous dot appearing in the cloudless portion of the night sky, especially with a fixed location relative to other such dots.
definitions.SKY: The atmosphere above a given point, especially as visible from the ground during the day.
definitions.DAWN: The morning twilight period immediately before sunrise.
definitions.DUSK: A period of time at the end of day when the sun is below the horizon but before the full onset of night, especially the darker part of twilight.
definitions.NIGHT: The period between sunset and sunrise, when a location faces far away from the sun, thus when the sky is dark.
definitions.DARK: Having an absolute or (more often) relative lack of light.
definitions.MOUNTAIN: A large natural elevation of the earth's surface rising abruptly from the surrounding level.
definitions.FOREST: A large area covered chiefly with trees and undergrowth.
definitions.JUNGLE: A large, undeveloped, humid forest, especially in a tropical region, that is home to many wild plants and animals; a tropical rainforest.
definitions.DESERT: A dry, sandy region with little rainfall and sparse vegetation.
definitions.ISLAND: A contiguous area of land, smaller than a continent, totally surrounded by water.
definitions.CANYON: A deep gorge, typically one with a river flowing through it.
definitions.VALLEY: A low area of land between hills or mountains, typically with a river.
definitions.PLATEAU: A largely level expanse of land at a high elevation; tableland.
definitions.PRAIRIE: An extensive area of relatively flat grassland with few, if any, trees, especially in North America.
definitions.MEADOW: A field of grass, often wildflowers, used for pasture or solace.
definitions.GLACIER: A slowly moving mass or river of ice formed by the accumulation of snow.
definitions.VOLCANO: A vent or fissure on the surface of a planet (usually in a mountainous form) with a magma chamber attached to the mantle of a planet or moon, periodically erupting forth lava and volcanic gases onto the surface.
definitions.GEYSER: A boiling natural spring which throws forth at frequent intervals jets of water, mud etc., driven up by the expansive power of steam.
definitions.WATERFALL: A flow of water over the edge of a cliff.
definitions.SPRINGS: To weaken, as a joint, ligament, or muscle, by sudden and excessive exertion, as by wrenching; to overstrain, or stretch injuriously, but without luxation.
definitions.MARSH: An area of low, wet land, often with tall grass.
definitions.SWAMP: A piece of wet, spongy land; low ground saturated with water; soft, wet ground which may have a growth of certain kinds of trees, but is unfit for agricultural or pastoral purposes.
definitions.BOG: An area of decayed vegetation (particularly sphagnum moss) which forms a wet spongy ground too soft for walking; a marsh or swamp.
definitions.TUNDRA: A vast, flat, treeless Arctic region where the subsoil is permanently frozen.
definitions.STEPPE: The grasslands of Eastern Europe and Asia.
definitions.RAINFOREST: A forest in a climate with high annual rainfall and no dry season.
definitions.SAVANNAH: A tropical grassland with scattered trees.
definitions.MANGROVE: Any of various tropical evergreen trees or shrubs that grow in shallow coastal water.
definitions.REEF: A chain or range of rocks, sand, or coral lying at or near the surface of the water.
definitions.ATOLL: A type of island consisting of a ribbon reef that nearly or entirely surrounds a lagoon and supports, in most cases, one to many islets on the reef platform.
definitions.PENINSULA: A piece of land projecting into water from a larger land mass.
definitions.CONTINENT: Each of the main continuous land-masses on the earth's surface, now generally regarded as seven in number, including their related islands, continental shelves etc.
definitions.PLANET: Each of the seven major bodies which move relative to the fixed stars in the night sky—the Moon, Mercury, Venus, the Sun, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn.
definitions.ATMOSPHERE: The gases surrounding the Earth or any astronomical body.
definitions.BIOSPHERE: The part of the Earth and its atmosphere capable of supporting life.
definitions.ECOSYSTEM: A system formed by an ecological community and its environment that functions as a unit.
definitions.HABITAT: Conditions suitable for an organism or population of organisms to live.
definitions.WILDLIFE: Animals, plants, and fungi, not normally domesticated, often to the exclusion of plants, fungi, fish, insects and other invertebrates, and microscopic plants and animals; hence:.
definitions.FLORA: Plants considered as a group, especially those of a particular country, region, time, etc.
definitions.FAUNA: Animals considered as a group; especially those of a particular country, region, time.
definitions.SURVIVAL: The fact or act of surviving.
definitions.CLIMATE: An area of the earth's surface between two parallels of latitude.
definitions.WEATHER: The short term state of the atmosphere at a specific time and place, including the temperature, relative humidity, cloud cover, precipitation, wind, etc.
definitions.SEASON: Each of the four divisions of a year: spring, summer, autumn (fall) and winter.
definitions.SPRING: To weaken, as a joint, ligament, or muscle, by sudden and excessive exertion, as by wrenching.
definitions.SUMMER: One of four seasons, traditionally the second, marked by the longest and typically hottest days of the year due to the inclination of the Earth and thermal lag.
definitions.AUTUMN: Traditionally the third of the four seasons, when deciduous trees lose their leaves.
definitions.WINTER: Traditionally the fourth of the four seasons, typically regarded as being from December 23 to March 20 in continental regions of the Northern Hemisphere or the months of June, July and August in the Southern Hemisphere.
definitions.EQUINOX: The intersection of the apparent path of the sun in the sky (the ecliptic) with the celestial equator.
definitions.SOLSTICE: One of the two points in the ecliptic at which the sun is furthest from the celestial equator.
definitions.ECLIPSE: An alignment of astronomical objects whereby one object comes between the observer (or notional observer) and another object, thus obscuring the latter.

definitions.CITY: A large settlement, bigger than a town.
definitions.ROAD: A way used for travelling between places, originally one wide enough to allow foot passengers and horses to travel, now (US) usually one surfaced with asphalt or concrete and designed to accommodate many vehicles travelling in both directions.
definitions.LANE: (used in street names) A road, street, or similar thoroughfare.
definitions.PARK: An area of land set aside for environment preservation or recreation.
definitions.YARD: A small, usually uncultivated area adjoining or (now especially) within the precincts of a house or other building.
definitions.FARM: A place where agricultural and similar activities take place, especially the growing of crops or the raising of livestock.
definitions.HILL: An elevated location smaller than a mountain.
definitions.PORT: The left side of a ship when facing forward.
definitions.SHOP: An establishment that sells goods or services to the public.
definitions.HOUSE: A structure built or serving as an abode of human beings.
definitions.CAFE: A convenience store, originally one that sold coffee and similar basic items.
definitions.BANK: An institution where one can place and borrow money and take care of financial affairs.
definitions.CLUB: An association of members joining together for some common purpose, especially sports or recreation.
definitions.GYM: A sports facility specialized for lifting weights and exercise.
definitions.MALL: A pedestrianised street, especially a shopping precinct.
definitions.AREA: A measure of the extent of a surface; it is measured in square units.
definitions.ZONE: Each of the five regions of the earth's surface into which it was divided by climatic differences, namely the torrid zone (between the tropics), two temperate zones (between the tropics and the polar circles), and two frigid zones (within the polar circles).
definitions.STATE: A condition; a set of circumstances applying at any given time.
definitions.LAND: The part of Earth which is not covered by oceans or other bodies of water.
definitions.WORLD: (with "the") Human collective existence; existence in general.
definitions.EARTH: The third planet of the Solar System; the world upon which humans live.
definitions.PLACE: (physical) An area; somewhere within an area.
definitions.SPOT: A round or irregular patch on the surface of a thing having a different color, texture etc. and generally round in shape.
definitions.BASE: Something from which other things extend; a foundation.
definitions.NORTH: One of the four major compass points, specifically 0°, directed toward the North Pole, and conventionally upwards on a map, abbreviated as N.
definitions.SOUTH: One of the four major compass points, specifically 180°, directed toward the South Pole, and conventionally downwards on a map, abbreviated as S.
definitions.EAST: One of the four principal compass points, specifically 90°, conventionally directed to the right on maps; the direction of the rising sun at an equinox.
definitions.WEST: One of the four principal compass points, specifically 270°, conventionally directed to the left on maps; the direction of the setting sun at an equinox, abbreviated as W.
definitions.BACK: The rear of the body, especially the part between the neck and the end of the spine and opposite the chest and belly.
definitions.FRONT: The foremost side of something or the end that faces the direction it normally moves.
definitions.HIGH: A high point or position, literally or figuratively; an elevated place; a superior region; a height; the sky; heaven.
definitions.LOW: Something that is low; a low point.
definitions.NEAR: The left side of a horse or of a team of horses pulling a carriage etc.
definitions.SCHOOL: (collective) A group of fish or a group of marine mammals such as porpoises, dolphins, or whales.
definitions.OFFICE: A ceremonial duty or service, particularly:.
definitions.STORE: A place where items may be accumulated or routinely kept.
definitions.MARKET: A gathering of people for the purchase and sale of merchandise at a set time, often periodic.
definitions.COUNTRY: (chiefly British) An area of land; a district, region.
definitions.NATION: A historically constituted, stable community of people, formed on the basis of a common language, territory, economic life, ethnicity and/or psychological make-up manifested in a common culture.
definitions.KINGDOM: A realm having a king and/or queen as its actual or nominal sovereign.
definitions.EMPIRE: (furniture) Following or imitating a style popular during the First French Empire (1804–1814).
definitions.REGION: Any considerable and connected part of a space or surface; specifically, a tract of land or sea of considerable but indefinite extent; a country; a district; in a broad sense, a place without special reference to location or extent but viewed as an entity for geographical, social or cultural reasons.
definitions.PROVINCE: A region of the earth or of a continent; a district or country.
definitions.COUNTY: The land ruled by a count or a countess.
definitions.DISTRICT: An administrative division of an area.
definitions.VILLAGE: A rural habitation of size between a hamlet and a town.
definitions.METROPOLIS: (history) The mother (founding) polis (city state) of a colony.
definitions.CAPITAL: Already-produced durable goods available for use as a factor of production, such as steam shovels (equipment) and office buildings (structures).
definitions.SUBURB: A residential area located on the outskirts of a city or large town that usually includes businesses that cater to its residents; such as schools, grocery stores, shopping centers, restaurants, convenience stores, etc.
definitions.NEIGHBORHOOD: The quality of being a neighbor, of living nearby, next to each-other; proximity.
definitions.COMMUNITY: A group sharing a common understanding, and often the same language, law, manners, and/or tradition.
definitions.STREET: A paved part of road, usually in a village or a town.
definitions.AVENUE: A broad street, especially one bordered by trees.
definitions.BOULEVARD: A broad, well-paved and landscaped thoroughfare.
definitions.HIGHWAY: A motor vehicle for transporting large numbers of people along roads.
definitions.FREEWAY: A road designed for safe, high-speed operation of motor vehicles through the elimination of at-grade intersections, usually divided and having at least two lanes in each direction; a dual carriageway with no at-grade crossings, a motorway.
definitions.AIRPORT: An airfield (an area designated for the takeoff and landing of aircraft), including one or more runways and (for commercial airports) one or more passenger terminals.
definitions.TERMINAL: A building in an airport where passengers transfer from ground transportation to the facilities that allow them to board airplanes.
definitions.MUSEUM: A building or institution dedicated to the acquisition, conservation, study, exhibition, and educational interpretation of objects having scientific, historical, cultural or artistic value.
definitions.LIBRARY: An institution which holds books and/or other forms of media for use by the public or qualified people often lending them out, as well as providing various other services for its users.
definitions.THEATER: A place or building, consisting of a stage and seating, in which an audience gathers to watch plays, musical performances, public ceremonies, and so on.
definitions.CINEMA: A movie theatre, a movie house.
definitions.STADIUM: A venue where sporting events are held.
definitions.UNIVERSITY: Institution of higher education (typically accepting students from the age of about 17 or 18, depending on country, but in some exceptional cases able to take younger students) where subjects are studied and researched in depth and degrees are offered.
definitions.ACADEMY: (usually capitalized) The garden where Plato taught.
definitions.INSTITUTE: An organization founded to promote a cause.
definitions.HOSPITAL: A large medical facility, usually in a building with multiple floors, where seriously ill or injured patients are given extensive medical and/or surgical treatment.
definitions.CLINIC: A medical facility, such as a hospital, especially one for the treatment and diagnosis of outpatients.
definitions.PHARMACY: (countable) A place where prescription drugs are dispensed.
definitions.FACTORY: A trading establishment, especially set up by merchants working in a foreign country.
definitions.WAREHOUSE: A place for storing large amounts of products.
definitions.DEPOT: A storage facility, in particular, a warehouse.
definitions.MOUNTAIN: A large natural elevation of the earth's surface rising abruptly from the surrounding level.
definitions.FOREST: A large area covered chiefly with trees and undergrowth.
definitions.DESERT: A dry, sandy region with little rainfall and sparse vegetation.
definitions.ISLAND: A contiguous area of land, smaller than a continent, totally surrounded by water.
definitions.BEACH: The shore of a body of water, especially when sandy or pebbly.
definitions.COAST: The edge of the land where it meets an ocean, sea, gulf, bay, or large lake.
definitions.VALLEY: A low area of land between hills or mountains, typically with a river.
definitions.CANYON: A deep gorge, typically one with a river flowing through it.
definitions.RIVER: A large and often winding stream which drains a land mass, carrying water down from higher areas to a lower point, oftentimes ending in another body of water, such as an ocean or in an inland sea.
definitions.LAKE: A small stream of running water; a channel for water; a drain.

definitions.ZEN: A state of calm attentiveness and intuitive peacefulness.
definitions.CALM: (in a person) The state of being calm.
definitions.PURE: One who, or that which, is pure.
definitions.DEEP: (with "the") The deep part of a lake, sea, etc.
definitions.KIND: A type, race or category; a group of entities that have common characteristics such that they may be grouped together.
definitions.TRUE: The state of being in alignment.
definitions.PEACE: A state of tranquility, quiet, and harmony; absence of violence.
definitions.STILL: A period of calm or silence.
definitions.SILENT: That which is silent; a time of silence.
definitions.BRIGHT: An artist's brush used in oil and acrylic painting with a long ferrule and a flat, somewhat tapering bristle head.
definitions.CLEAR: Full extent; distance between extreme limits; especially; the distance between the nearest surfaces of two bodies, or the space between walls.
definitions.FRESH: A rush of water, along a river or onto the land; a flood.
definitions.FLOW: A movement in people or things with a particular way in large numbers or amounts.
definitions.MOVE: The act of moving; a movement.
definitions.RISE: To move, or appear to move, physically upwards relative to the ground.
definitions.FALL: The act of moving to a lower position under the effect of gravity.
definitions.BREATH: The act or process of breathing.
definitions.SPIRIT: The soul of a person or other creature.
definitions.HEART: A muscular organ that pumps blood through the body, traditionally thought to be the seat of emotion.
definitions.SOUL: The spirit or essence of a person usually thought to consist of one's thoughts and personality.
definitions.LIFE: The state of organisms preceding their death, characterized by biological processes such as metabolism and reproduction and distinguishing them from inanimate objects; the state of being alive and living.
definitions.DREAM: Imaginary events seen in the mind while sleeping.
definitions.HOPE: To want something to happen, with a sense of expectation that it might.
definitions.WISH: A desire, hope, or longing for something or for something to happen.
definitions.SMILE: A facial expression comprised by flexing the muscles of both ends of one's mouth, often showing the front teeth, without vocalisation, and in humans is a common involuntary or voluntary expression of happiness, pleasure, amusement or anxiety.
definitions.REST: (of a person or animal) Relief from work or activity by sleeping; sleep.
definitions.SLEEP: To rest in a state of reduced consciousness.
definitions.WAKE: The act of waking, or state of being awake.
definitions.LIVE: To be alive; to have life.
definitions.GIVE: The amount of bending that something undergoes when a force is applied to it; a tendency to yield under pressure; resilence.
definitions.TAKE: The or an act of taking.
definitions.HELP: Action given to provide assistance; aid.
definitions.SHARE: A portion of something, especially a portion given or allotted to someone.
definitions.HEAL: A spell or ability that restores hit points or removes a status ailment.
definitions.MEDITATE: To contemplate; to keep the mind fixed upon something; to study.
definitions.FOCUS: A point at which reflected or refracted rays of light converge.
definitions.BALANCE: A state in which opposing forces harmonise; equilibrium.
definitions.TRANQUIL: Free from emotional or mental disturbance.
definitions.JOY: A feeling of extreme happiness or cheerfulness, especially related to the acquisition or expectation of something good.
definitions.WISDOM: An element of personal character that enables one to distinguish the wise from the unwise.
definitions.TRUTH: True facts, genuine depiction or statements of reality.
definitions.UNITY: Oneness; the state or fact of being one undivided entity.
definitions.FREEDOM: The state of being free, of not being imprisoned or enslaved.
definitions.STILLNESS: The quality or state of being still.
definitions.CALMNESS: The state of being calm; tranquillity; silence.
definitions.HUMBLE: (Baltimore) An arrest based on weak evidence intended to demean or punish the subject.
definitions.COMPASSION: Deep awareness of the suffering of another, coupled with the wish to relieve it.
definitions.EMPATHY: Identification with or understanding of the thoughts, feelings, or emotional state of another person.
definitions.ONENESS: State of being one or undivided.
definitions.PRESENCE: The fact or condition of being present, or of being within sight or call, or at hand.
definitions.AWARENESS: The state or level of consciousness where sense data can be confirmed by an observer.
definitions.INSIGHT: A sight or view of the interior of anything.
definitions.VISION: The sense or ability of sight.
definitions.CLARITY: The state or measure of being clear, either in appearance, thought or style.
definitions.ENERGY: The impetus behind all motion and all activity.
definitions.SPIRITUAL: A Christian religious song, especially one in an African-American style, or a similar non-religious song.
definitions.COSMIC: Of or from or pertaining to the cosmos or universe.
definitions.INFINITE: Something that is infinite in nature.
definitions.SACRED: Characterized by solemn religious ceremony or religious use, especially, in a positive sense.
definitions.HOLY: A thing that is extremely holy.
definitions.ANCIENT: A person who is very old.
definitions.TIMELESS: A gene encoding an essential protein that regulates circadian rhythm, normally written in italics: timeless.
definitions.AWAKEN: To become conscious after having slept.
definitions.NIRVANA: A transcendent state of ultimate peace, liberation, and freedom.
definitions.SAMADHI: A state of deep meditative absorption and spiritual oneness.
definitions.SATORI: A state of sudden spiritual enlightenment or awakening.
definitions.MANTRA: A sacred sound or phrase repeated to aid concentration in meditation.
definitions.CHANT: A rhythmic singing or speaking of words to quiet the mind.
definitions.OM: A sacred cosmic sound representing the essence of the universe.
definitions.SHANTI: A Sanskrit word representing peace, calmness, and tranquility.
definitions.NAMASTE: A respectful greeting expressing honor and spiritual connection.
